answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a bond-and-audit scheme. Before an agent can mine, it locks a stake and signs a pledge with a quill, and the ledger keeps a public mirror of every pledge. Each epoch the protocol randomly audits a slice of agents and demands proof that the identity is real; a failure slashes the bond into a shared harbor fund. To pass as N agents an attacker must post N independent bonds and hope none of his clones get sampled, so the expected loss grows linearly with the number of fake identities he creates.
